Bill number: HB6004
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 6001
 By Johnson

 HOUSE BILL 6004

 By Lamberth

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 4,
 Chapter 49; Title 8 and Title 49, relative to the
 Education Freedom Act of 2025.

 WHEREAS, publicly supported educational freedom has a long history in Tennessee,

with the Hope Scholarship providing funding that follows students to the public or private

institution of their choice; and

 WHEREAS, parents should be free to choose the school that best fits the educational

needs of their specific child; and

 WHEREAS, Tennessee has worked to expand choice through the successful education

savings account pilot program that is now helping primarily underserved, minority students in

three of the State's largest school districts with 99% parent satisfaction with the program; and

 WHEREAS, over the past six years, Tennessee has invested a record $2 billion annually

in additional state dollars for public education; and

 WHEREAS, high-quality educational facilities and high-performing teachers are vital

ingredients for a child's success; and

 WHEREAS, the "Education Freedom Scholarship Act" will empower parents with the

freedom to choose the right education for their child and provide parents a say in where their

taxpayer dollars are spent; now, therefore,

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. This act is known and may be cited as the "Education Freedom Act of

2025."

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 6, is amended by adding

the following as a new part:

49-6-3501. Short title.

 This part is known and may be cited as the "Education Freedom Scholarship

Act."

49-6-3502. Part definitions.

 As used in this part, unless the context otherwise requires:

 (1) "Department" means the department of education;

 (2) "Eligible student" means a resident of this state who is entitled to

 attend a public school, except for a student enrolled in a home school, as defined

 in § 49-6-3050, or in a church-related school, as defined in § 49-50-801, with

 which the student's parent is associated, registered, or is participating as a

 parent-teacher for purposes of § 49-6-3050(a)(2) or (a)(3);

 (3) "Parent" means the parent, guardian, person who has custody of the

 child, or individual who has caregiving authority for the child under § 49-6-3001;

 (4) "Private school" means a school that is:

 (A) Located in this state; and

 (B) A private school, as defined in § 49-6-3001(c)(3)(A), that is a

 category I, II, or III school approved by the commissioner of education in

 accordance with rules promulgated by the state board of education;

 (5) "Program" means the education freedom scholarship program

 created by this part;

 (6) "Public school" means a public charter school, a school operated by

 an LEA, or a school operated by this state with public funds that serves students

 in any of the grades kindergarten through twelve (K-12);

 (7) "Recipient" means an eligible student who enrolls in a private school

 and receives a scholarship for a given school year; and

 (8) "Scholarship" means an education freedom scholarship provided

 pursuant to this part.

49-6-3503. Creation.

 (a) There is created an education freedom scholarship program to be

administered by the department.

 (b) Subject to appropriations and other available funds, the program must

provide a scholarship to an eligible student who applies for the 2025-2026 school year or

any subsequent school year, subject to the limitations of this part.

49-6-3504. Scholarship availability – prioritization of awards.

 (a) For the 2025-2026 school year, the department shall award a maximum of

twenty thousand (20,000) scholarships, to be awarded as follows, in the order in which

the department receives completed scholarship applications:

 (1) Ten thousand (10,000) scholarships are available for eligible students

 who meet one (1) of the following criteria:

 (A) The student's annual household income does not exceed

 three hundred percent (300%) of the amount required for the student to

 qualify for free or reduced price lunch, as provided in the income eligibility

 guidelines published by the United States department of agriculture's food

 and nutrition service; or

 (B) The student is an eligible student as defined in § 49-6-2602 or

 § 49-10-1402; and

 (2) Ten thousand (10,000) scholarships are available for eligible

 students, regardless of whether the eligible student meets one (1) of the criteria

 listed in subdivision (a)(1).

 (b) Beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, and subject to the funds

appropriated for scholarships together with any available funds returned to the state

treasurer pursuant to § 49-6-3506, if the number of applications received by the

department during a program application period:

 (1) Exceeds seventy-five percent (75%) of the total number of

 scholarships available for the respective school year, then the department may

 increase the maximum number of scholarships available for the next school year

 by no more than five thousand (5,000) additional scholarships; or

 (2) Does not exceed seventy-five percent (75%) of the total number of

 scholarships available for the respective school year, then the maximum number

 of scholarships available for the next school year must remain the same as the

 maximum number of scholarships available for the prior school year.

 (c) Beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, if the number of applications

received by the department exceeds the number of scholarships available for the

respective school year, then the department shall award scholarships in the following

order:

 (1) An eligible student who received a scholarship in the immediately

 preceding school year;

 (2) An eligible student whose annual household income does not exceed

 one hundred percent (100%) of the amount required for the student to qualify for

 free or reduced price lunch, as provided in the income eligibility guidelines

 published by the United States department of agriculture's food and nutrition

 service, or an eligible student who is an eligible student as defined in § 49-6-

 2602 or § 49-10-1402, in the order in which the department receives completed

 scholarship applications;

 (3) An eligible student whose annual household income does not exceed

 three hundred percent (300%) of the amount required for the student to qualify

 for free or reduced price lunch, as provided in the income eligibility guidelines

 published by the United States department of agriculture's food and nutrition

 service, in the order in which the department receives completed scholarship

 applications;

 (4) An eligible student who, at the time of submitting a completed

 application, is currently enrolled in a public school, or who is eligible to enroll in

 kindergarten in a public school for the respective school year, in the order in

 which the department receives completed scholarship applications; and

 (5) An eligible student, in the order in which the department receives

 completed scholarship applications.

 (d) In order to receive a scholarship under this part, an eligible student, or the

eligible student's parent, must:

 (1) Submit a completed scholarship application to the department;

 (2) Ensure the provision of an education for the eligible student that

 satisfies the compulsory school attendance requirement provided in § 49-6-

 3001(c)(1) through enrollment in a private school; and

 (3) Not enroll the eligible student in a kindergarten through grade twelve

 (K-12) public school in any school year for which the eligible student receives a

 scholarship.

 (e) The department may award a scholarship to an eligible student in an order

that does not comply with the order prescribed in subsection (a) or subsection (c), as

applicable, if awarding the scholarship out of order is consistent with the outcome of an

administrative appeal adjudicating the denial of the student's scholarship application.

49-6-3505. Scholarship amounts – allowable uses.

 (a) A scholarship equals the base funding amount, as defined in § 49-3-104(2),

and is solely state funded.

 (b) Scholarship funds must first be used to pay the recipient's tuition and fees, as

described in subdivision (c)(1). Any outstanding scholarship funds available to the

recipient after payment of tuition and fees may be used for one (1) or more of the

educational expenses described in subdivisions (c)(2) – (c)(8).

 (c) Scholarship funds may only be used for the following educational expenses:

 (1) Tuition and fees required by the private school in which the recipient

 is enrolled;

 (2) Textbooks, curricula, instructional materials, and uniforms required by

 the private school in which the recipient is enrolled;

 (3) Tutoring services provided by a tutor or tutoring facility that meets the

 requirements established by the department;

 (4) Fees for transportation to and from the private school in which the

 recipient is enrolled, paid to a fee-for-service transportation provider that meets

 the requirements established by the department;

 (5) Computer hardware, technological devices, and other technology

 fees that meet the requirements established by the department and that are used

 for the recipient's educational needs;

 (6) Tuition, fees, textbooks, curricula, and instructional materials for

 summer academic programs and specialized afterschool academic programs

 that meet the requirements established by the department. This subdivision

 (c)(6) does not include afterschool childcare;

 (7) Fees for early postsecondary opportunity courses or examinations,

 entrance examinations required for postsecondary admission, and industry

 credentials as approved by the department; and

 (8) Educational therapy services provided by therapists who meet the

 requirements established by the department.

49-6-3506. Unspent funds – account closure.

 (a) A recipient's scholarship account remains open, and all available scholarship

funds remain in the recipient's scholarship account, from one (1) school year to another

unless one (1) of the events described in subsection (b) occurs.

 (b) A recipient's scholarship account must be closed, and all remaining

scholarship funds returned to the state treasurer to be used to award scholarships to

eligible students in future years pursuant to this part, upon the earlier of:

 (1) The recipient's graduation from high school or obtainment of a high

 school equivalency credential approved by the state board of education;

 (2) The recipient's enrollment in a kindergarten through grade twelve (K-

 12) public school;

 (3) The recipient's completion of thirteen (13) school years as a

 kindergarten through grade twelve (K-12) student;

 (4) The recipient's voluntary withdrawal from the scholarship program; or

 (5) The department disqualifying the recipient from participating in the

 program due to the recipient's noncompliance with program requirements.

49-6-3507. Administration of assessments for recipients.

 (a) As a condition of receiving a scholarship pursuant to this part, recipients in

grades three through eleven (3-11) must be annually administered:

 (1) A nationally standardized achievement test that is aligned to the

 respective private school's instructional plan, as determined by rules promulgated

 by the state board of education; or

 (2) The Tennessee comprehensive assessment program test required for

 the grade in which the recipient is enrolled.

 (b) Each private school that enrolls recipients shall annually administer the test

required pursuant to subsection (a) to the recipients enrolled in the school. Each private

school shall provide the results of the test administered to a recipient pursuant to

subsection (a) to the recipient's parents.

 (c) By June 30, 2026, and by each June 30 thereafter, each private school shall

provide the results of the tests administered to recipients pursuant to subsection (a) to

the office of research and education accountability in the office of the comptroller of the

treasury. A private school may provide the test results required pursuant to this

subsection (c) using aggregated, deidentified data; provided, that the data must be

provided on a form developed by the office of research and education accountability in a

manner that allows the office of research and educational accountability to group and

analyze the results by recipient grade level, household income level, sex, and race. The

office of research and education accountability shall submit an annual report to the

education committees of the senate and house of representatives detailing the results of

the tests administered to recipients pursuant to subsection (a).

49-6-3508. Autonomy of schools that have recipients enrolled.

 (a) A private school that enrolls recipients is autonomous and not an agent of

this state.

 (b) The creation of the education freedom scholarship program does not expand

the regulatory authority of this state, the officers of this state, or the authority of any LEA

to impose any additional rules, regulations, or requirements on private schools that enroll

recipients beyond the rules narrowly tailored to enforce the requirements of the program.

 (c) Private schools that enroll recipients must have the maximum freedom to

provide for the educational needs of recipients without governmental control. A private

school that enrolls recipients is not required to alter its creed, practices, admission

policies, hiring policies, or curriculum in order to accept recipients.

49-6-3509. Limitations on participation – connection to other education programs.

 (a) Notwithstanding another law to the contrary, the department shall deny a

scholarship to an eligible student for the same school year in which the student is

participating in the Tennessee education savings account pilot program, compiled in part

26 of this chapter, or the individualized education account program, compiled in chapter

10, part 14 of this title.

 (b) A recipient does not retain the right to receive special education and related

services from the LEA in which the recipient resides, through an individualized education

program. Recipients have the same rights under the Individuals with Disabilities

Education Act (IDEA) (20 U.S.C. § 1414) to receive equitable services through an

individualized service plan as all other students enrolled in non-public schools.

49-6-3510. Payment – state or local public benefit.

 (a) A scholarship awarded under this part:

 (1) Shall not be paid directly to a recipient or recipient's parent; and

 (2) Is a state or local public benefit under § 4-58-102.

 (b) Funds received pursuant to this part do not constitute income taxable to the

parent of the recipient or to the recipient under title 67, chapter 2.

49-6-3511. Denial of scholarship application.

 Notwithstanding § 49-6-3504, the department shall deny the scholarship

 application of an eligible student who cannot establish the eligible student's lawful

 presence in the United States.

 49-6-3512. Promulgation of rules.

 The department shall promulgate rules to effectuate this part. The rules must

 include an administrative appeal procedure for the denial of scholarship applications.

 The rules must be promulgated in accordance with the Uniform Administrative

 Procedures Act, compiled in title 4, chapter 5.

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-108, is amended by adding the

following as a new subsection:

 (i)

 (1) Beginning with the TISA allocation for the 2025-2026 year, and

 except when subdivision (i)(2) applies, if an LEA's TISA allocation for the current

 school year is less than the LEA's TISA allocation for the immediately preceding

 school year, and if the LEA experienced disenrollment, then the department shall

 allocate additional funds to the LEA such that the LEA's TISA allocation for the

 current school year combined with the amount of any additional funds received

 by the LEA pursuant to this subdivision (i)(1) is equal to the LEA's TISA allocation

 for the immediately preceding school year.

 (2) Beginning with the TISA allocation for the 2026-2027 school year, if

 an LEA has ever received additional funds under this subsection (i), and if an

 LEA's TISA allocation for the current school year is less than the sum total of the

 LEA's TISA allocation for the immediately preceding school year and the amount

 of any additional funds received by the LEA pursuant to this subsection (i) for the

 immediately preceding school year, and if the LEA experienced disenrollment,

 then the department shall allocate additional funds to the LEA such that the

 LEA's TISA allocation for the current school year is equal to the sum total of the

 LEA's TISA allocation for the immediately preceding school year and the amount

 of any additional funds received by the LEA pursuant to this subsection (i) for the

 immediately preceding school year.

 (3) Any additional funds provided to an LEA pursuant to this subsection

 (i) must be solely state funded. If an LEA is eligible for additional funds under

 this subsection (i) and subsection (b) or (c), then the department shall only award

 additional funds to the LEA pursuant to this subsection (i) and shall not award

 any additional funds to the LEA pursuant to subsection (b) or (c).

 (4) As used in this subsection (i), "disenrollment" means that the LEA's

 non-virtual average daily membership for the current school year is lower than

 the LEA's non-virtual average daily membership for the immediately preceding

 school year.

SECTION 4.

 (a) Subject to appropriation, the department of education shall award a one-time

bonus in the amount of two thousand dollars ($2,000) to each teacher employed in a

kindergarten through grade twelve (K-12) public school in this state for the 2024-2025

school year.

 (b)

 (1) A bonus awarded pursuant to this section is solely state funded.

 (2) Bonuses paid to teachers pursuant to this section are not part of the

 TISA, as defined in § 49-3-104, and must not be considered salary payments or

 supplements for purposes of § 49-3-306.

 (c) For purposes of this section, "teacher" has the same meaning as "existing

 educator," as that term is defined in § 49-3-104.

 SECTION 5. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 4-49-104(e)(1), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting instead:

 (1) Eighty percent (80%) of the privilege tax collected under this section must be

 distributed by the council to the state treasurer for deposit into an account administered

 by the state treasurer for use by local education agencies, as defined in § 49-1-103, for

 the construction and maintenance of public school buildings. When allocating funds for

 such purpose, the state treasurer shall consider:

 (A) Whether the local education agency is located in a county that is

 designated as an economically distressed or at-risk county by the department of

 economic and community development;

 (B) The occurrence of any emergency or natural disaster that has

 resulted in significant damage to an existing public school building or facility; and

 (C) Other demonstrated need, as identified by the local education

 agency.

 SECTION 6. If any provision of this act or its application to any person or circumstance

is held invalid, then the invalidity does not affect other provisions or applications of the act that

can be given effect without the invalid provision or application, and to that end, the provisions of

this act are severable.

 SECTION 7. The headings in this act are for reference purposes only and do not

constitute a part of the law enacted by this act. However, the Tennessee Code Commission is

requested to include the headings in any compilation or publication containing this act.

 SECTION 8. Section 5 of this act takes effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring

it. All other sections of this act take effect upon becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
The bill would create a state-funded education freedom scholarship program for eligible Tennessee students to attend approved private schools in the state. A student must be a Tennessee resident entitled to attend public school. Students enrolled in a home school, or in a church-related school under the parent arrangements specified in the bill, would not qualify. To receive a scholarship, a student or parent must apply, enroll the student in a private school that satisfies compulsory attendance requirements, and keep the student out of a K–12 public school during the scholarship year. The department of education would administer the program, subject to available funding, and adopt rules that include an appeal process for denied applications.

For 2025–2026, the department could award up to 20,000 scholarships in order of completed applications. Half would be reserved for students whose household income is no more than 300% of the amount required to qualify for free or reduced-price lunch, or who meet either of two eligibility definitions cited in the bill. The other half would be open to all eligible students. In later years, the department could raise the next year’s limit by up to 5,000 if applications exceed 75% of available scholarships and funds are available; otherwise, the limit would stay the same. If applications exceed available scholarships, priority would go first to prior-year recipients, then to students in the bill’s lowest-income or cited eligibility groups, then to students under the 300% income threshold, then to current public school students and students eligible to enter public kindergarten, and finally to other eligible students. The department could award out of order to comply with an appeal decision.

Each scholarship would equal the base funding amount cited in the bill. It must pay private-school tuition and fees first. Remaining funds could pay for specified school materials and uniforms, qualifying tutoring and transportation, educational technology, qualifying summer and afterschool academic programs, certain courses, exams and credentials, and qualifying educational therapy. Unspent funds would carry over until an account-closing event, such as graduation, public-school enrollment, withdrawal or disqualification. Remaining funds would then return to the state treasurer for future scholarships. Scholarships could not be paid directly to students or parents. The department would deny an application if the student could not establish lawful presence in the United States, and could not award a scholarship for a year in which the student participates in either of two other education account programs named in the bill.

Scholarship recipients in grades 3–11 would take an annual qualifying standardized test or the applicable Tennessee assessment. Participating private schools would give parents the results and, beginning June 30, 2026, report results annually to the comptroller’s office of research and education accountability, which would report to legislative education committees. The bill would limit additional state regulation of participating private schools and would not require them to change their creed, practices, admissions, hiring or curriculum. It also specifies that recipients would not retain a right to special education services from their local education agency through an individualized education program, while retaining the equitable-service rights described in the bill.

Separately, beginning in 2025–2026, the bill would provide additional state funds to a local education agency whose TISA allocation falls and whose non-virtual average daily membership declines, under the bill’s stated calculation. It would provide a one-time, $2,000 state-funded bonus, subject to appropriation, for each qualifying public-school teacher employed in 2024–2025. It would also direct 80% of the privilege tax collected under the cited section to an account for public-school building construction and maintenance, with specified needs considered in allocating funds. That tax provision would take effect July 1, 2025; the rest of the bill would take effect upon becoming law.
</summary>

Subject to appropriations and other available funds, the program must

provide a scholarship to an eligible student who applies
claims.rationale: Scholarship provision is expressly subject to appropriations and other available funds.

claims.claim: The department must adopt rules including an appeal process for denied applications.
claims.summary_quote: adopt rules that include an appeal process for denied applications
claims.source_quote:
The department shall promulgate rules to effectuate this part. The rules must

 include an administrative appeal procedure for the denial of scholarship applications.
claims.rationale: Both rulemaking and an administrative appeal procedure are required.

claims.claim: The 2025–2026 scholarship cap would be 20,000.
claims.summary_quote: For 2025–2026, the department could award up to 20,000 scholarships
claims.source_quote:
For the 2025-2026 school year, the department shall award a maximum of

twenty thousand (20,000) scholarships
claims.rationale: The summary accurately states the maximum available, subject to the program's funding and eligibility conditions.

claims.claim: Initial-year awards generally follow the order of completed applications.
claims.summary_quote: in order of completed applications
claims.source_quote:
in the order in which

the department receives completed scholarship applications
claims.rationale: This is the prescribed order, with the appeal exception separately acknowledged in the summary.

claims.claim: Half the initial scholarships would be reserved for students meeting the 300% income criterion or either cited eligibility definition.
claims.summary_quote: Half would be reserved for students whose household income is no more than 300% of the amount required to qualify for free or reduced-price lunch, or who meet either of two eligibility definitions cited in the bill.
claims.source_quote:
Ten thousand (10,000) scholarships are available for eligible students

 who meet one (1) of the following criteria:

 (A) The student's annual household income does not exceed

 three hundred percent (300%) of the amount required for the student to

 qualify for free or reduced price lunch, as provided in the income eligibility

 guidelines published by the United States department of agriculture's food

 and nutrition service; or

 (B) The student is an eligible student as defined in § 49-6-2602 or

 § 49-10-1402;
claims.rationale: Ten thousand is half the initial cap, and the alternative qualifications are accurately described without expanding the cited statutes.

claims.claim: The other half of the initial scholarships would be available to all eligible students.
claims.summary_quote: The other half would be open to all eligible students.
claims.source_quote:
Ten thousand (10,000) scholarships are available for eligible

 students, regardless of whether the eligible student meets one (1) of the criteria

 listed in subdivision (a)(1).
claims.rationale: The second allocation does not require the reserved allocation's additional criteria.

claims.claim: In later years, available funding and applications exceeding 75% of available scholarships permit a next-year increase of no more than 5,000.
claims.summary_quote: In later years, the department could raise the next year’s limit by up to 5,000 if applications exceed 75% of available scholarships and funds are available
claims.source_quote:
Beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, and subject to the funds

appropriated for scholarships together with any available funds returned to the state

treasurer pursuant to § 49-6-3506, if the number of applications received by the

department during a program application period:

 (1) Exceeds seventy-five percent (75%) of the total number of

 scholarships available for the respective school year, then the department may

 increase the maximum number of scholarships available for the next school year

 by no more than five thousand (5,000) additional scholarships;
claims.rationale: The summary preserves the discretionary increase, numerical cap, application trigger, and funding condition.

claims.claim: Otherwise, the scholarship limit would remain unchanged.
claims.summary_quote: otherwise, the limit would stay the same
claims.source_quote:
Does not exceed seventy-five percent (75%) of the total number of

 scholarships available for the respective school year, then the maximum number

 of scholarships available for the next school year must remain the same as the

 maximum number of scholarships available for the prior school year.
claims.rationale: The bill requires an unchanged cap when applications do not exceed the threshold and conditions any increase on available funds.

claims.claim: In later oversubscribed years, prior-year recipients receive first priority.
claims.summary_quote: If applications exceed available scholarships, priority would go first to prior-year recipients
claims.source_quote:
Beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, if the number of applications

received by the department exceeds the number of scholarships available for the

respective school year, then the department shall award scholarships in the following

order:

 (1) An eligible student who received a scholarship in the immediately

 preceding school year;
claims.rationale: In the paragraph's later-year context, this correctly describes the trigger and first priority.

claims.claim: The next priority is the lowest-income or cited eligibility groups.
claims.summary_quote: then to students in the bill’s lowest-income or cited eligibility groups
claims.source_quote:
An eligible student whose annual household income does not exceed

 one hundred percent (100%) of the amount required for the student to qualify for

 free or reduced price lunch, as provided in the income eligibility guidelines

 published by the United States department of agriculture's food and nutrition

 service, or an eligible student who is an eligible student as defined in § 49-6-

 2602 or § 49-10-1402
claims.rationale: The second priority covers the lower income threshold and the two cited eligibility definitions.

claims.claim: The third priority is students meeting the 300% income threshold.
claims.summary_quote: then to students under the 300% income threshold
claims.source_quote:
(3) An eligible student whose annual household income does not exceed

 three hundred percent (300%) of the amount required for the student to qualify

 for free or reduced price lunch
claims.rationale: This refers to the 300% threshold previously described as inclusive in the summary.

claims.claim: The fourth priority is current public-school students and students eligible for public kindergarten.
claims.summary_quote: then to current public school students and students eligible to enter public kindergarten
claims.source_quote:
(4) An eligible student who, at the time of submitting a completed

 application, is currently enrolled in a public school, or who is eligible to enroll in

 kindergarten in a public school for the respective school year
claims.rationale: The summary correctly identifies the fourth-priority groups.

claims.claim: Other eligible students receive final priority.
claims.summary_quote: and finally to other eligible students
claims.source_quote:
(5) An eligible student, in the order in which the department receives

 completed scholarship applications.
claims.rationale: The final priority is the general eligible-student category.

claims.claim: The department may award out of order consistently with an appeal decision.
claims.summary_quote: The department could award out of order to comply with an appeal decision.
claims.source_quote:
The department may award a scholarship to an eligible student in an order

that does not comply with the order prescribed in subsection (a) or subsection (c), as

applicable, if awarding the scholarship out of order is consistent with the outcome of an

administrative appeal adjudicating the denial of the student's scholarship application.
claims.rationale: The summary preserves the department's permission and the appeal-related condition.

claims.claim: Each scholarship equals the cited base funding amount.
claims.summary_quote: Each scholarship would equal the base funding amount cited in the bill.
claims.source_quote: A scholarship equals the base funding amount, as defined in § 49-3-104(2)
claims.rationale: The amount is correctly described without supplying an unsupported dollar figure.

claims.claim: Scholarship funds must pay private-school tuition and fees first.
claims.summary_quote: It must pay private-school tuition and fees first.
claims.source_quote:
Scholarship funds must first be used to pay the recipient's tuition and fees, as

described in subdivision (c)(1).
claims.rationale: The bill expressly gives tuition and fees first priority.

claims.claim: Remaining funds may pay for specified school materials and uniforms.
claims.summary_quote: Remaining funds could pay for specified school materials and uniforms
claims.source_quote:
Textbooks, curricula, instructional materials, and uniforms required by

 the private school in which the recipient is enrolled;
claims.rationale: These are authorized expenses after tuition and fees have been paid.

claims.claim: Remaining funds may pay for qualifying tutoring.
claims.summary_quote: qualifying tutoring and transportation
claims.source_quote:
Tutoring services provided by a tutor or tutoring facility that meets the

 requirements established by the department;
claims.rationale: Tutoring is permitted when the provider meets department requirements.

claims.claim: Remaining funds may pay for qualifying transportation.
claims.summary_quote: qualifying tutoring and transportation
claims.rationale: The bill authorizes qualifying transportation expenses.

claims.claim: Remaining funds may pay for educational technology.
claims.summary_quote: educational technology
claims.rationale: Educational technology is an authorized expense category.

claims.claim: Remaining funds may pay for qualifying summer and afterschool academic programs.
claims.summary_quote: qualifying summer and afterschool academic programs
claims.source_quote:
Tuition, fees, textbooks, curricula, and instructional materials for

 summer academic programs and specialized afterschool academic programs

 that meet the requirements established by the department.
claims.rationale: The summary accurately limits this category to qualifying academic programs.

claims.claim: Remaining funds may pay for certain courses, examinations, and credentials.
claims.summary_quote: certain courses, exams and credentials
claims.rationale: The bill authorizes these specified fees.

claims.claim: Remaining funds may pay for qualifying educational therapy.
claims.summary_quote: qualifying educational therapy
claims.source_quote:
Educational therapy services provided by therapists who meet the

 requirements established by the department.
claims.rationale: Educational therapy from qualifying therapists is authorized.

claims.claim: Unspent scholarship funds carry over until an account-closing event.
claims.summary_quote: Unspent funds would carry over until an account-closing event
claims.source_quote:
A recipient's scholarship account remains open, and all available scholarship

funds remain in the recipient's scholarship account, from one (1) school year to another

unless one (1) of the events described in subsection (b) occurs.
claims.rationale: The bill expressly allows funds to remain across school years until a listed event.

claims.claim: Graduation is an account-closing event.
claims.summary_quote: such as graduation
claims.source_quote:
The recipient's graduation from high school or obtainment of a high

 school equivalency credential approved by the state board of education;
claims.rationale: High-school graduation is expressly listed.

claims.claim: Public-school enrollment is an account-closing event.
claims.summary_quote: public-school enrollment
claims.source_quote:
The recipient's enrollment in a kindergarten through grade twelve (K-

 12) public school;
claims.rationale: In this K–12 program context, the summary correctly identifies the enrollment trigger.

claims.claim: Withdrawal from the program is an account-closing event.
claims.summary_quote: withdrawal or disqualification
claims.source_quote: The recipient's voluntary withdrawal from the scholarship program;
claims.rationale: Voluntary program withdrawal closes the account.

claims.claim: Disqualification from the program is an account-closing event.
claims.summary_quote: withdrawal or disqualification
claims.source_quote:
The department disqualifying the recipient from participating in the

 program due to the recipient's noncompliance with program requirements.
claims.rationale: The bill lists departmental disqualification for noncompliance.

claims.claim: Funds remaining when an account closes return to the state treasurer for future scholarships.
claims.summary_quote: Remaining funds would then return to the state treasurer for future scholarships.
claims.source_quote:
A recipient's scholarship account must be closed, and all remaining

scholarship funds returned to the state treasurer to be used to award scholarships to

eligible students in future years
claims.rationale: Both the return and future scholarship use are expressly required.

claims.claim: Scholarships cannot be paid directly to recipients or their parents.
claims.summary_quote: Scholarships could not be paid directly to students or parents.
claims.source_quote: Shall not be paid directly to a recipient or recipient's parent;
claims.rationale: The bill expressly prohibits direct payment.

claims.claim: The department must deny an application when the student cannot establish lawful presence in the United States.
claims.summary_quote: The department would deny an application if the student could not establish lawful presence in the United States
claims.source_quote:
the department shall deny the scholarship

 application of an eligible student who cannot establish the eligible student's lawful

 presence in the United States.
claims.rationale: The summary correctly states the mandatory denial and its condition.

claims.claim: A scholarship cannot be awarded for a year in which the student participates in either of the two named education account programs.
claims.summary_quote: could not award a scholarship for a year in which the student participates in either of two other education account programs named in the bill
claims.source_quote:
the department shall deny a

scholarship to an eligible student for the same school year in which the student is

participating in the Tennessee education savings account pilot program, compiled in part

26 of this chapter, or the individualized education account program, compiled in chapter

10, part 14 of this title.
claims.rationale: The prohibition covers same-year participation in either named program.

claims.claim: Recipients in grades 3–11 must take an annual qualifying standardized test or the applicable Tennessee assessment.
claims.summary_quote: Scholarship recipients in grades 3–11 would take an annual qualifying standardized test or the applicable Tennessee assessment.
claims.source_quote:
recipients in

grades three through eleven (3-11) must be annually administered:

 (1) A nationally standardized achievement test that is aligned to the

 respective private school's instructional plan, as determined by rules promulgated

 by the state board of education; or

 (2) The Tennessee comprehensive assessment program test required for

 the grade in which the recipient is enrolled.
claims.rationale: The grades, frequency, and alternative assessments match the bill.

claims.claim: Participating private schools must provide test results to parents.
claims.summary_quote: Participating private schools would give parents the results
claims.source_quote:
Each private

school shall provide the results of the test administered to a recipient pursuant to

subsection (a) to the recipient's parents.
claims.rationale: The bill assigns this duty to the private school.

claims.claim: Private schools must report results annually to the comptroller's office of research and education accountability, starting with June 30, 2026.
claims.summary_quote: beginning June 30, 2026, report results annually to the comptroller’s office of research and education accountability
claims.source_quote:
By June 30, 2026, and by each June 30 thereafter, each private school shall

provide the results of the tests administered to recipients pursuant to subsection (a) to

the office of research and education accountability in the office of the comptroller of the

treasury.
claims.rationale: The summary identifies the correct first reporting date, annual frequency, and receiving office.

claims.claim: That office must report test results to legislative education committees.
claims.summary_quote: which would report to legislative education committees
claims.source_quote:
The

office of research and education accountability shall submit an annual report to the

education committees of the senate and house of representatives detailing the results of

the tests administered to recipients pursuant to subsection (a).
claims.rationale: The bill requires a report to both chambers' education committees.

claims.claim: The bill limits additional state regulation of participating private schools.
claims.summary_quote: The bill would limit additional state regulation of participating private schools
claims.source_quote:
The creation of the education freedom scholarship program does not expand

the regulatory authority of this state, the officers of this state, or the authority of any LEA

to impose any additional rules, regulations, or requirements on private schools that enroll

recipients beyond the rules narrowly tailored to enforce the requirements of the program.
claims.rationale: The bill restricts additional regulatory authority to narrowly tailored program-enforcement rules.

claims.claim: Participating schools need not change their creed, practices, admissions, hiring, or curriculum to accept recipients.
claims.summary_quote: would not require them to change their creed, practices, admissions, hiring or curriculum
claims.source_quote:
A private

school that enrolls recipients is not required to alter its creed, practices, admission

policies, hiring policies, or curriculum in order to accept recipients.
claims.rationale: Every listed protected aspect appears in the bill.

claims.claim: Recipients do not retain the right to special education services from their resident local education agency through an individualized education program.
claims.summary_quote: recipients would not retain a right to special education services from their local education agency through an individualized education program
claims.source_quote:
A recipient does not retain the right to receive special education and related

services from the LEA in which the recipient resides, through an individualized education

program.
claims.rationale: This accurately describes the bill's stated loss of the IEP-based entitlement.

claims.claim: Recipients retain the equitable-service rights described in the bill.
claims.summary_quote: while retaining the equitable-service rights described in the bill
claims.source_quote:
Recipients have the same rights under the Individuals with Disabilities

Education Act (IDEA) (20 U.S.C. § 1414) to receive equitable services through an

individualized service plan as all other students enrolled in non-public schools.
claims.rationale: The summary does not expand the rights beyond the bill's express statement.

claims.claim: Beginning in 2025–2026, the bill provides additional funds under its calculation to an agency experiencing a TISA allocation decline and a decline in non-virtual average daily membership.
claims.summary_quote: beginning in 2025–2026, the bill would provide additional state funds to a local education agency whose TISA allocation falls and whose non-virtual average daily membership declines, under the bill’s stated calculation
claims.source_quote:
Beginning with the TISA allocation for the 2025-2026 year, and

 except when subdivision (i)(2) applies, if an LEA's TISA allocation for the current

 school year is less than the LEA's TISA allocation for the immediately preceding

 school year, and if the LEA experienced disenrollment, then the department shall

 allocate additional funds to the LEA
claims.rationale: The summary accurately describes the initial trigger and expressly defers to the bill's calculation, which includes the later-year rule.

claims.claim: The enrollment decline relevant to that funding is a decline in non-virtual average daily membership.
claims.summary_quote: whose non-virtual average daily membership declines
claims.source_quote:
"disenrollment" means that the LEA's

 non-virtual average daily membership for the current school year is lower than

 the LEA's non-virtual average daily membership for the immediately preceding

 school year.
claims.rationale: The summary uses the bill's express definition of disenrollment.

claims.claim: The additional agency funds are state funded.
claims.summary_quote: additional state funds
claims.source_quote:
Any additional funds provided to an LEA pursuant to this subsection

 (i) must be solely state funded.
claims.rationale: The bill expressly requires exclusive state funding.

claims.claim: The bill provides a one-time $2,000 teacher bonus.
claims.summary_quote: It would provide a one-time, $2,000 state-funded bonus
claims.source_quote:
the department of education shall award a one-time

bonus in the amount of two thousand dollars ($2,000)
claims.rationale: The amount and one-time nature match the bill.

claims.claim: The teacher bonus is state funded.
claims.summary_quote: state-funded bonus
claims.source_quote: A bonus awarded pursuant to this section is solely state funded.
claims.rationale: The bill expressly makes the bonus solely state funded.

claims.claim: The teacher bonus is subject to appropriation.
claims.summary_quote: subject to appropriation
claims.source_quote:
Subject to appropriation, the department of education shall award a one-time

bonus
claims.rationale: The summary preserves the funding condition.

claims.claim: Each qualifying public-school teacher employed in 2024–2025 would receive the bonus.
claims.summary_quote: for each qualifying public-school teacher employed in 2024–2025
claims.source_quote:
to each teacher employed in a

kindergarten through grade twelve (K-12) public school in this state for the 2024-2025

school year.
claims.rationale: The school year and recipient group match; 'qualifying' accommodates the bill's teacher definition.

claims.claim: The bill directs 80% of the privilege tax under the cited section to a public-school construction and maintenance account.
claims.summary_quote: It would also direct 80% of the privilege tax collected under the cited section to an account for public-school building construction and maintenance
claims.source_quote:
Eighty percent (80%) of the privilege tax collected under this section must be

 distributed by the council to the state treasurer for deposit into an account administered

 by the state treasurer for use by local education agencies, as defined in § 49-1-103, for

 the construction and maintenance of public school buildings.
claims.rationale: The percentage, tax reference, destination, and permitted purpose match the bill.

claims.claim: Specified needs must be considered in allocating the construction and maintenance funds.
claims.summary_quote: with specified needs considered in allocating funds
claims.source_quote:
When allocating funds for

 such purpose, the state treasurer shall consider:

 (A) Whether the local education agency is located in a county that is

 designated as an economically distressed or at-risk county by the department of

 economic and community development;

 (B) The occurrence of any emergency or natural disaster that has

 resulted in significant damage to an existing public school building or facility; and

 (C) Other demonstrated need, as identified by the local education

 agency.
claims.rationale: The bill requires consideration of the specified circumstances and demonstrated needs.

claims.claim: The tax provision takes effect July 1, 2025.
claims.summary_quote: That tax provision would take effect July 1, 2025
claims.source_quote: Section 5 of this act takes effect July 1, 2025
claims.rationale: Section 5 contains the privilege-tax allocation provision.

claims.claim: The rest of the bill takes effect upon becoming law.
claims.summary_quote: the rest of the bill would take effect upon becoming law
claims.source_quote: All other sections of this act take effect upon becoming a law
claims.rationale: The bill expressly gives all other sections this effective date.
